# Goal

when chatlog is loaded, auto scroll to end, keep it sticky at end while it is at end

# Current state

`ActionPopupContent` provides the chat scroll container. `ActionConversationChat` renders the selected or live conversation, but neither component tracks whether the viewport is at the end. Loading a conversation and streaming new content therefore leave the scroll position unchanged.

# Implementation details

- Make `ActionConversationChat` own its scroll viewport and bottom-stick state.
- Treat a viewport within a small tolerance of its maximum scroll position as being at the end.
- Start at the end when a conversation loads or the selected conversation changes.
- After messages or streamed assistant content grow, scroll to the end only when the viewport was already at the end.
- Update stickiness on user scroll. Scrolling up stops automatic movement; returning to the end enables it again.
- Keep empty and shorter-than-viewport conversations at the end without errors.

# Acceptance criteria

- Opening or selecting a conversation shows its latest content.
- New messages and streamed content remain visible while the chat is at the end.
- New content does not move the viewport after the user scrolls up.
- Scrolling back to the end restores sticky behavior.
- Behavior is shared by card and project agent popups.
- Component tests cover initial load, conversation changes, content growth, opt-out, and reactivation.

# Architectural decisions

Project-wide decisions for MDÂ². The app is a Vite React web app in `app/`; `desktop/` is a separate Electron host that can load the website and expose local capabilities through preload bridges.

## File naming

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Code files use lowercase snake_case names. | All code files in `app/src/` and `desktop/` use lowercase words separated by underscores, for example `github_auth_service.ts`, `project_workspace.tsx`, and `local_git_service.js`. Test files keep the same base name with `.test` before the extension, for example `github_auth_service.test.ts`. Exported symbols keep normal TypeScript/JavaScript casing such as `GithubAuthService`, `ProjectWorkspace`, and `useGithubAuth`. | A single file naming convention avoids mixed PascalCase, camelCase, and hyphenated filenames, and keeps imports predictable across Windows and case-sensitive environments. |

## Services and state

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Global singleton services own domain state and logic. | Each domain is a class in `src/services/**`, instantiated once at module level and exported, for example `export const indexesService = new IndexesService()`. React components do not own domain state. | Keeps business logic out of components, testable without a DOM, and shared across windows/views without Redux, Zustand, or Context stores. |
| Service location follows usage scope. | If a service is specific to one UI element and used only there, place it beside that component. Generic or shared services, such as logging, database access, config, storage, or cross-screen domain logic, belong in `src/services/`. | Keeps component-owned behavior local while preserving `src/services/` for reusable application services. |
| Consumers use direct imports or the service injector. | Direct import when no import cycle exists; use `src/services/service_injector.js` when a cycle would occur. Every global singleton service registers itself in its constructor with `inj.register('myService', this)`. | The service graph is dense; the injector is a bare global registry that defers resolution to call time. |
| Services have a two-phase lifecycle. | Constructors only register and set unloaded state such as `null`. Config-dependent or service-dependent work runs in `init()`, `start()`, app bootstrap (`App.jsx`), or a `loaded` lifecycle event. `configService.config` is private; callers use `get`, `set`, and `clear`. | Module evaluation order is not guaranteed, so `configService` is not usable at import time. Reading config in a constructor is a bug. |


## Events and React integration

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Services notify observers through their own `EventTarget`. | Services expose an `EventTarget` and dispatch named `CustomEvent` domain events such as `activeIndex`, `added`, `deleted`, or `changedBox`. Observers subscribe with `addEventListener` and unsubscribe with `removeEventListener` on the owning service. | Decouples producers from consumers without depending on Node `EventEmitter`, which is not available in the browser-first React app. |
| Custom hooks bridge service events to functional components. | Hooks in `src/components/hooks/`, such as `useActiveIndex` and `useProjectConfig`, seed `useState` from a service property, subscribe in `useEffect`, unsubscribe in cleanup, and return the value. Prefer hook + service over prop chains. | Components stay declarative and avoid direct event plumbing. |
| Components subscribe at the smallest rendering boundary. | Root and layout components compose UI regions and pass structural inputs. Components that render changing application data subscribe through hooks themselves. Do not hoist changing data into ancestors only to pass it downward. | Limits rerenders to affected UI, protects transient state such as open popups, and avoids broad prop chains. |
| Components use the app theme service path. | `App` owns theme mode through `useThemeMode()`, builds the MUI theme with `createAppTheme(mode)`, and provides it through `ThemeProvider`. Components read theme values with MUI APIs such as `useTheme`, `useMediaQuery`, and `sx`; only controls that change the palette mode receive `mode` and `onToggleTheme`. | Theme state, persistence, and palette construction stay centralized while components remain presentation-focused. |

# Architectural decisions

Project-wide decisions for MDÂ². The app is a Vite React web app in `app/`; `desktop/` is a separate Electron host that can load the website and expose local capabilities through preload bridges.

## File naming

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Code files use lowercase snake_case names. | All code files in `app/src/` and `desktop/` use lowercase words separated by underscores, for example `github_auth_service.ts`, `project_workspace.tsx`, and `local_git_service.js`. Test files keep the same base name with `.test` before the extension, for example `github_auth_service.test.ts`. Exported symbols keep normal TypeScript/JavaScript casing such as `GithubAuthService`, `ProjectWorkspace`, and `useGithubAuth`. | A single file naming convention avoids mixed PascalCase, camelCase, and hyphenated filenames, and keeps imports predictable across Windows and case-sensitive environments. |

## Services and state

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Global singleton services own domain state and logic. | Each domain is a class in `src/services/**`, instantiated once at module level and exported, for example `export const indexesService = new IndexesService()`. React components do not own domain state. | Keeps business logic out of components, testable without a DOM, and shared across windows/views without Redux, Zustand, or Context stores. |
| Service location follows usage scope. | If a service is specific to one UI element and used only there, place it beside that component. Generic or shared services, such as logging, database access, config, storage, or cross-screen domain logic, belong in `src/services/`. | Keeps component-owned behavior local while preserving `src/services/` for reusable application services. |
| Consumers use direct imports or the service injector. | Direct import when no import cycle exists; use `src/services/service_injector.js` when a cycle would occur. Every global singleton service registers itself in its constructor with `inj.register('myService', this)`. | The service graph is dense; the injector is a bare global registry that defers resolution to call time. |
| Services have a two-phase lifecycle. | Constructors only register and set unloaded state such as `null`. Config-dependent or service-dependent work runs in `init()`, `start()`, app bootstrap (`App.jsx`), or a `loaded` lifecycle event. `configService.config` is private; callers use `get`, `set`, and `clear`. | Module evaluation order is not guaranteed, so `configService` is not usable at import time. Reading config in a constructor is a bug. |


## Events and React integration

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Services notify observers through their own `EventTarget`. | Services expose an `EventTarget` and dispatch named `CustomEvent` domain events such as `activeIndex`, `added`, `deleted`, or `changedBox`. Observers subscribe with `addEventListener` and unsubscribe with `removeEventListener` on the owning service. | Decouples producers from consumers without depending on Node `EventEmitter`, which is not available in the browser-first React app. |
| Custom hooks bridge service events to functional components. | Hooks in `src/components/hooks/`, such as `useActiveIndex` and `useProjectConfig`, seed `useState` from a service property, subscribe in `useEffect`, unsubscribe in cleanup, and return the value. Prefer hook + service over prop chains. | Components stay declarative and avoid direct event plumbing. |
| Components subscribe at the smallest rendering boundary. | Root and layout components compose UI regions and pass structural inputs. Components that render changing application data subscribe through hooks themselves. Do not hoist changing data into ancestors only to pass it downward. | Limits rerenders to affected UI, protects transient state such as open popups, and avoids broad prop chains. |
| Components use the app theme service path. | `App` owns theme mode through `useThemeMode()`, builds the MUI theme with `createAppTheme(mode)`, and provides it through `ThemeProvider`. Components read theme values with MUI APIs such as `useTheme`, `useMediaQuery`, and `sx`; only controls that change the palette mode receive `mode` and `onToggleTheme`. | Theme state, persistence, and palette construction stay centralized while components remain presentation-focused. |

design\activity\card__31eb5a7b-6d2b-407c-a83f-8e6c9c0201f3.json:136:          "content": "---\nid: F-052\ntitle: agent popup conversation layout, history picker and full-height mode\nstatus: ready\nowner: JB\naffects:\npolicy:\n  checkLinting: true\n  requireTests: true\ninternalId: 9929944d-5218-4bdc-bdf8-f7e3fdf59723\n---\n\n## Goal\n\nMake the agent popup read like a chat: show the selected conversation above the prompt, replace the inline agent run-history list with a conversation picker, and allow the popup to expand to the full application height.\n\n## Current state\n\n`ActionPopup` is shared by the card `Run` entry point and the project agent FAB. In its card-run layout, `ActionAgentForm` renders the Agent, Model and Thinking selectors followed immediately by the prompt. `ActionRunStatus` is rendered below the form and shows phase summaries rather than the persisted conversation messages. `ActionRunHistory` then renders every action-history entry inline.\n\nAction history is keyed by action id and context and stores output summaries; an entry has no conversation reference and therefore cannot load a chat. Persisted `AgentConversation` records already contain `startedAt`, `title`, `messages` and `path`, but card conversations are discovered through the card's `agents` frontmatter and project-scoped conversations have no equivalent listing contract. The parser also replaces a missing conversation title with its id, so the UI cannot currently distinguish an explicit title from a fallback.\n\n## Implementation details\n\n### Agent popup layout\n\n- Apply the new layout to agent actions in both shared popup entry points: card `Run` and the project agent FAB. Command-action history and its diff controls keep their current behavior.\n- Keep Agent, Model and Thinking on one control row. Add a conversation-history dropdown on that row and align it to the right.\n- Below the controls, show the selected conversation as an ordered chat log using its user and assistant messages. The active run continues to stream into this area; lifecycle, tool and error events may be shown where relevant without replacing the message transcript with phase summaries.\n- Place a divider below the chat log and the prompt input below the divider. Empty/new conversations show an empty chat area without an inline run-history placeholder.\n- Starting a new conversation selects its live log. Selecting a persisted conversation loads it by reference and replaces the displayed chat log. If the user continues that conversation, pass the selected conversation `path` through the existing `continueFrom` flow; do not continue a different or merely most-recent conversation.\n- Loading failures use `dialogService` and leave the previously selected conversation visible.\n\n### Conversation history dropdown\n\n- Replace `ActionRunHistory` in the agent popup with the dropdown; do not derive the picker from `ActionRunHistoryEntry` summaries.\n- Each item represents exactly one persisted `AgentConversation` belonging to the popup context. Card popups include conversations whose stable `cardInternalId` matches the card. Project popups include project-scoped conversations whose `cardInternalId` is `null`. Do not mix conversations from another card or scope.\n- Sort conversations newest first by `startedAt` and display the date and local time for every item.\n- When the log contains a non-empty explicit `title`, use it as the item text and show the date/time with it. Without an explicit title, use the date/time as the item text. Preserve whether the title was explicit during parsing instead of presenting the current id fallback as a title.\n- Add a listing/loading boundary that works for local Git, GitHub and remote-control storage. Card frontmatter references can remain the card discovery source; project scope needs an explicit way to discover its conversation references. Keep path validation and stable `cardInternalId` ownership checks.\n- Refresh the picker after a run is persisted. A running conversation may appear immediately, but it must not be duplicated when the persisted record arrives.\n\n### Full-height mode\n\n- Add an `Expand upward` icon button immediately before the existing Close button in the popup header.\n- Expanding detaches the popup's positioning from its FAB or card `Run` anchor while retaining the selected action and context. Position its top and bottom edges at the application viewport edges so it occupies the full application height; preserve its current width and horizontal position within the viewport.\n- In full-height mode, replace the expand button with a `Collapse downward` button. Height resize handles are inactive while expanded.\n- Collapsing reattaches the popup to its original anchor and restores the exact pre-expansion size and placement. Full-height dimensions must not overwrite the separately persisted normal sizes for card and project-agent popups.\n- Closing from full-height mode closes normally. Reopening starts in normal anchored mode. Resizing the application while expanded keeps the popup constrained to the application height.\n\n## Affected components\n\n- `app/src/components/actions/action_popup.tsx`: header controls, agent-only layout, selected chat and expanded state.\n- `app/src/components/actions/action_agent_form.tsx`: separate the selector row and prompt so the chat and divider can sit between them without duplicating form behavior.\n- `app/src/components/actions/use_action_popup_controller.ts`: conversation selection/loading, refresh and continuation reference.\n- `app/src/components/actions/action_run_history.tsx`: remains for command actions; it is no longer rendered for agent actions.\n- `app/src/components/resizable_popper.tsx`: support a controlled full-height detached presentation while preserving normal anchored size.\n- Agent conversation types, parsers and storage/bridge implementations: retain explicit-title information and list conversations for the requested context.\n\n## Edge cases\n\n- An empty history leaves the dropdown empty/disabled and still allows a new run.\n- Invalid dates fall back to the stored timestamp text rather than hiding the conversation.\n- Switching actions reloads and selects history for the new action/context; a late response from the previous selection must not replace it.\n- A selected failed or cancelled conversation remains readable. Continuation availability follows the existing provider/session rules.\n- Expanding a card-linked popup changes only presentation; it does not lose or broaden the card context.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- In an agent popup, the selected/live chat is above the prompt and a divider separates them.\n- Agent, Model and Thinking remain on one row, with a right-aligned conversation dropdown.\n- Every dropdown item shows local date and time; an explicit log title is used as its label when present.\n- Selecting an item loads that single conversation into the chat, and continuing uses that conversation's reference.\n- Card and project popups show only conversations owned by their context and refresh without duplicates after a run.\n- Agent popups no longer show the inline `ActionRunHistory`; command history and diff behavior are unchanged.\n- The header shows Expand immediately before Close. Expand fills the application height and detaches from the anchor; Collapse restores the original anchored size and placement.\n- Tests cover layout order, divider placement, title/date fallback labels, sorting, context filtering, selection races and errors, continuation reference, history refresh, expand/collapse restoration, viewport resizing, and both card and FAB entry points.\n- App and desktop lint, typecheck and tests pass.\n\n## See also\n\n- `design/architecture/initial description/action_popup.md`\n- `design/feature_descriptions/F_049_agent_chat_fab_popup.md`\n- `design/feature_descriptions/ready/F_047_running_actions_and_agents.md`\n- `design/feature_descriptions/ready/F_050_one_shot_agent_conversations.md`\n- `design/feature_descriptions/ready/F_033_agent_and_model_selection.md`\n\r\n",

The app is a Vite React web app in `app/`; `desktop/` is a separate Electron host that can load the website and expose local capabilities through preload bridges.\n\n## File naming\n\n| Decision | Rule | Rationale |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| Code files use lowercase snake_case names. | All code files in `app/src/` and `desktop/` use lowercase words separated by underscores, for example `github_auth_service.ts`, `project_workspace.tsx`, and `local_git_service.js`. Exported symbols keep normal TypeScript/JavaScript casing such as `GithubAuthService`, `ProjectWorkspace`, and `useGithubAuth`. | A single file naming convention avoids mixed PascalCase, camelCase, and hyphenated filenames, and keeps imports predictable across Windows and case-sensitive environments. |\n\n## Services and state\n\n| Decision | Rule | Rationale |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| Global singleton services own domain state and logic. | Each domain is a class in `src/services/**`, instantiated once at module level and exported, for example `export const indexesService = new IndexesService()`. React components do not own domain state. | Keeps business logic out of components, testable without a DOM, and shared across windows/views without Redux, Zustand, or Context stores. |\n| Service location follows usage scope. | If a service is specific to one UI element and used only there, place it beside that component. Generic or shared services, such as logging, database access, config, storage, or cross-screen domain logic, belong in `src/services/`. | Keeps component-owned behavior local while preserving `src/services/` for reusable application services. |\n| Consumers use direct imports or the service injector. | Direct import when no import cycle exists; use `src/services/service_injector.js` when a cycle would occur. Every global singleton service registers itself in its constructor with `inj.register('myService', this)`. | The service graph is dense; the injector is a bare global registry that defers resolution to call time. |\n| Services have a two-phase lifecycle. | Constructors only register and set unloaded state such as `null`. Config-dependent or service-dependent work runs in `init()`, `start()`, app bootstrap (`App.jsx`), or a `loaded` lifecycle event. `configService.config` is private; callers use `get`, `set`, and `clear`. | Module evaluation order is not guaranteed, so `configService` is not usable at import time. Reading config in a constructor is a bug. |\n\n\n## Events and React integration\n\n| Decision | Rule | Rationale |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| Services notify observers through their own `EventTarget`. | Services expose an `EventTarget` and dispatch named `CustomEvent` domain events such as `activeIndex`, `added`, `deleted`, or `changedBox`. Observers subscribe with `addEventListener` and unsubscribe with `removeEventListener` on the owning service. | Decouples producers from consumers without depending on Node `EventEmitter`, which is not available in the browser-first React app. |\n| Custom hooks bridge service events to functional components. | Hooks in `src/components/hooks/`, such as `useActiveIndex` and `useProjectConfig`, seed `useState` from a service property, subscribe in `useEffect`, unsubscribe in cleanup, and return the value. Prefer hook + service over prop chains. | Components stay declarative and avoid direct event plumbing. |\n| Components subscribe at the smallest rendering boundary. | Root and layout components compose UI regions and pass structural inputs. Components that render changing application data subscribe through hooks themselves. (\n                    <Button\n                        disabled={runDisabled}\n                        onClick={handlePrimaryRun}\n                        size=\"small\"\n                        startIcon={<Play sx={{ fontSize: '13px !important' }} />}\n                        sx={{ height: 34, px: 2 }}\n                        variant=\"contained\"\n                    >\n                        Run\n                    </Button>\n                ) : null}\n            </Box>\n        </ResizablePopper>\n    )\n}\n\r\n---\ninternalId: f2ec9e28-8064-4707-bce9-b62f24d57524\n---\n\n# App Style Guide â€” Kanban / MDÂ² (React + MUI)\n\nHow to build **any new component** so it matches the app. This is written for **Material UI v5+** components.\n\n**The theme is the source of truth.** All color, radius, base typography, and spacing units live in the single `createTheme` (defined in `GUIDANCE.md` Â§1/Â§9). This guide does **not** define colors â€” it tells you **which theme value to use for which role**, and covers the things the theme can't encode: layout, spacing/margins, borders, elevation, and component conventions.\n\n**The one rule that matters:** never write a raw hex, px radius, or magic color into a component. Read it from the theme (`theme.palette.*`, `theme.shape`, `theme.typography`, `theme.spacing`). If a component has a hardcoded hex in its `sx`/styled, it's wrong â€” that's exactly where the look drifts and where dark mode breaks.\n\n---\n\n## 1. How to consume the theme\n\n- **Colors:** `sx={{ color: 'text.secondary', bgcolor: 'background.paper', borderColor: 'divider' }}` â€” MUI resolves dotted palette paths automatically in `sx`. In `styled`/JS use the callback form: `styled(Box)(({ theme }) => ({ color: theme.palette.text.secondary }))`.\n- **Spacing:** use the 8px unit via the spacing scale â€” `sx={{ p: 2, gap: 1, mt: 1.5 }}` (`2` = 16px, `1` = 8px). Don't write `padding: '16px'`.\n- **Radius:** `borderRadius: 1` (= `theme.shape.borderRadius` = 8) and multiples; for the fixed non-8 radii see Â§4.\n- **Typography:** prefer `Typography variant=...` and `theme.typography.*` over ad-hoc `fontSize`.\n- **Custom tokens:** roles the default MUI palette doesn't cover (column/track surfaces, the strong/hover border steps, `text-3/4`, section-header color, `primary-bg` tint, status colors) must exist in the theme under a namespace (e.g. `theme.palette.custom.*`) with light + dark values. Consume them the same way â€” `bgcolor: 'custom.column'`. **Never inline their hex.** If a needed token doesn't exist yet, add it to the theme, don't hardcode it in the component.\n\n---\n\n## 2. Role â†’ theme slot\n\nPick the slot by the element's **role**, not by how it looks in one mode:\n\n| Role | Theme slot |\n|---|---|\n| App background; tinted footer/action bars | `background.default` |\n| Column & sidebar surface | `custom.column` |\n| Segmented-control / toolbar track, hover fill | `custom.track` |\n| Card, dialog, popup, input surface | `background.paper` |\n| Hairlines, resting borders | `divider` |\n| Input borders, vertical separators | `custom.borderStrong` |\n| Border on hover | `custom.borderHover` |\n| Titles, values, headings | `text.primary` |\n| Body copy, field labels | `text.secondary` |\n| Meta, captions, resting icons | `custom.text3` |\n| Muted / placeholder / disabled | `custom.text4` |\n| Uppercase section/column headers | `custom.colHead` |\n| The one CTA, selection, focus, links, icon-hover | `primary.main` |\n| Contained-button hover | `primary.dark` |\n| Selected/tinted bg, focus ring, ID-chip bg | `custom.primaryBg` |\n| Text/icon on a primary fill | `primary.contrastText` |\n| Active / saved / online dot | `success.main` |\n| Destructive action | `error.main` |\n| Status swatch dots & ID-chip tints (decorative only) | `custom.status.*` |\n\nRules: **one** `primary` per surface (the CTA/selection accent) â€” everything else is `text-*`/`divider`. Status colors are **decoration only** (dots, chip tints), never interactive color. Dark-mode brightness/tinting is handled inside the theme's two palettes, so a correctly-sloted component needs zero per-mode code.\n\n---\n\n## 3. Layout\n\n- **Full-height app:** column flex â€” menu row / ribbon / content (`flex: 1; minHeight: 0`) / status bar. Fixed bands `flexShrink: 0`.\n- **Board:** horizontal-scroll flex row, `gap: 2` (16px), page padding `p: 2.5` (20px); columns `width: 296, flexShrink: 0`, internal column flex `gap: 1`.\n- **List view:** two-pane flex row filling the space between ribbon and status bar â€” sidebar `width: 280, flexShrink: 0`, editor pane `flex: 1, minWidth: 0` (the `minWidth: 0` is required so long content ellipsizes instead of blowing out the row).\n- **Panels (sidebar, editor card, dialogs):** column flex with stacked bands (header / [toolbar] / body / footer). The **body scrolls** (`overflow-y: auto; minHeight: 0`); header and footer are `flexShrink: 0` and never scroll away.\n- **Spacer pattern:** push trailing items with `<Box sx={{ flex: 1 }} />` rather than `margin-left: auto` sprinkled around, so rows stay predictable.\n- Use flex `gap` for spacing between siblings â€” don't hand-space with per-child margins.\n\n---\n\n## 4. Spacing, margin & size conventions\n\n- **4/8px grid, via `theme.spacing`.** page padding `2.5`; between columns `2`; inside columns / between related controls `1`; dialog body gap `2â€“2.25`; field labelâ†’control gap `~0.9` (7px).\n- **Margins:** prefer padding on containers + flex `gap` over element margins. Where a floating panel needs breathing room (e.g. editor card, toolbar inside a panel), use container padding (`p: 2 / 2.5`), not margins on the children.\n- **Fixed heights (px):** menu row 44, ribbon 52, status bar 32, section header 40, tab row 40, standard button / control 34, dense icon button 26â€“28, input 42.\n- **Fixed widths (px):** column 296, sidebar 280, search 260, standard dialog 480, wide/editor dialog 760.\n- **Radius family (px):** buttons/icon-buttons 8 (small 6â€“7), inputs 9, cards 10, columns/panels 12, dialogs/popups 14, chips/pills 99, color swatches 3. `borderRadius: 1` covers the 8 case; use explicit `'9px'` etc. for the others.\n\n---\n\n## 5. Borders & elevation\n\n- **Rest = border, not shadow.** Resting surfaces: `border: '1px solid'`, `borderColor: 'divider'`. Inputs use `custom.borderStrong`. **Shadow only when floating or lifted** (hover, drag, dialogs/popovers).\n- **Separation between bands:** a single 1px `divider` hairline. Don't stack a heavy rule *and* an outline â€” one line, let background contrast do the rest. Vertical separators inside toolbars: a 20px-tall `custom.borderStrong` rule.\n- **Elevation ladder (only where floating):** card hover `0 4px 12px rgba(16,24,40,0.12)`; dragging MUI `elevation 8` + `rotate(2deg)`; contained button `0 1px 2px rgba(16,24,40,0.15)`; dialog/popup `0 24px 60px rgba(16,24,40,0.28)`; scrim `rgba(16,24,40,0.45)` + `backdropFilter: blur(2px)`.\n- Set `MuiPaper.elevation: 0` and `MuiButton.disableElevation` globally in the theme; add the shadows above explicitly where the ladder calls for it.\n- **On dark backgrounds shadows read as nothing** â€” the theme already handles this by making hover raise `borderColor` (`custom.borderHover`) instead of relying on shadow.\n\n---\n\n## 6. Typography usage\n\nDrive everything from theme variants / `theme.typography`; avoid ad-hoc `fontSize`.\n\n- Titles/values/headings â†’ `text.primary`; body & labels â†’ `text.secondary`; meta â†’ `custom.text3`.\n- **Field labels:** a plain `Typography` (12px/600, `text.secondary`) placed **above** the control â€” **never** MUI floating/outlined `TextField` labels (they clash with the app's flat-label style).\n- **Section/column headers:** `Typography variant=\"overline\"` (uppercase, `letterSpacing ~0.7px`, `fontWeight 700`, `custom.colHead`).\n- **ID chips only** use monospace; everything else is the theme's default family.\n- `button.textTransform: 'none'` and `button.fontWeight: 600` are set in the theme â€” don't re-uppercase buttons.\n\n---\n\n## 7. Interaction states\n\nConsistent across all components; all colors from the theme:\n\n- **Ghost icon button** (`IconButton`): transparent â†’ hover `bgcolor: track` (or `background.paper` on a colored panel) + `color: primary.main`. Override MUI's default circular hover tint via `sx`.\n- **Outlined button:** `divider` border, `text.secondary` â†’ hover `borderColor/color: primary.main`. Destructive: hover `borderColor: error.main` + `bgcolor: custom.dangerBg`.\n- **Contained (primary) CTA:** `primary.main` + small shadow â†’ hover `primary.dark`.\n- **Input/field focus:** `borderColor: primary.main` + `boxShadow: 0 0 0 3px` in `custom.primaryBg` (the soft halo). Unfocused hover: `borderColor: custom.borderHover`.\n- **List/tree row:** hover `bgcolor: track`; selected `bgcolor: custom.primaryBg` + title `text.primary`.\n- **Row-level actions** (delete, â‹®): hidden at rest, shown on `:hover`/`:focus-within` via **opacity** (keep in DOM so width doesn't jump).\n- **Active tab/menu item:** 2px `primary.main` bottom border + `primary.main` text.\n- Every icon-only control gets a `Tooltip` (theme sets `arrow: true`) **and** an `aria-label`.\n\n---\n\n## 8. Component conventions (MUI primitives)\n\n- **Buttons:** `Button variant=\"contained\"` = the single CTA per surface; `variant=\"outlined\"` = secondary; `variant=\"text\"` = tertiary. Icon-only â†’ `IconButton` in a `Tooltip`. Don't use `Link` or text `Button` where an action button belongs (that reproduces the old text-link look).\n- **Icons:** `@mui/icons-material` **Outlined** variants; `fontSize: 18` in 34px buttons, `16` in dense, `13â€“15` inline. Don't hand-draw SVG.\n- **ID chip:** monospace, accent text on `custom.primaryBg`/status tint, `radius 5, flexShrink: 0`.\n- **Count chip:** `background.paper` bg, 1px `divider`, radius 9â€“10, `custom.text3`.\n- **State dot:** 7â€“8px circle + `text-3` label; green (`success.main`) = active/saved/online.\n- **Search:** pill `TextField` (`borderRadius: 99`, `bgcolor: background.default`), search start-adornment, `âŒ˜K` keycap end-adornment.\n- **Select:** `size=\"small\"`, optional dot+name via `renderValue`; 42px / radius-9 frame. When a select has a tooltip, keep the tooltip available while the select is closed and explicitly hide it for the entire time the select menu is open so it cannot cover the first option.\n- **Segmented control** (view switch, formatting toolbar): `ToggleButtonGroup` on a `custom.track` background; selected segment `background.paper` + `0 1px 2px` shadow + `primary` text.\n- **Dialog / popup:** `Dialog`/`Popover` with `PaperProps` â†’ `background.paper`, 1px `divider`, radius 14, big shadow; scrim via `slotProps.backdrop` (blur + tint). Bands separated by hairlines; footer on a `background.default` bar with top hairline; actions right-aligned (outlined Cancel + contained CTA). `autoFocus` first field; submit on `Enter` (`âŒ˜/Ctrl+Enter` in a textarea); close on `Esc`/backdrop.\n- **Empty state:** dashed target â€” `1.5px dashed custom.borderStrong`, radius 10, centered icon + `custom.text4` label. No \"click to add\" placeholder blocks.\n\n---\n\n## 9. Definition of done for a new component\n\n1. Zero hardcoded hex / raw px colors â€” every value comes from `theme.palette` / `theme.shape` / `theme.spacing` / `theme.typography`.\n2. Correct roleâ†’slot mapping (Â§2); at most one `primary` CTA on the surface.\n3. Borders at rest, shadow only when floating (Â§5); bands split by a single hairline.\n4. Hover **and** focus states on every interactive element (Â§7); icon buttons have tooltip + `aria-label`.\n5. Body scrolls, header/footer pinned; `minWidth: 0` on flex children that hold long text.\n6. Toggle to dark mode and confirm nothing breaks â€” if it does, you hardcoded a color somewhere (Â§1).\n\nComponent-specific detail lives in `GUIDANCE.md` (theme definition + board/list/dialog), `CARD_POPUP_GUIDE.md`, `RUN_DIALOG_GUIDE.md`, and `SIDEBAR_ACTIONS_GUIDE.md`.\n\r\n",

useEffect, useMemo, useRef, useState, useSyncExternalStore } from 'react'\r\nimport { navigateTo } from '../../app/app_navigation'\r\nimport { CONFIG_SECTIONS, configService, type ConfigEntry, type ConfigKey } from '../../services/config/config_service'\r\nimport { writeDesktopConfigToBridge } from '../../services/config/config_persistence'\r\nimport { dataService } from '../../services/data/data_service'\r\nimport { dialogService } from '../../services/dialog_service'\r\nimport { DesktopConfigSection } from './desktop_config_section'\r\nimport { ProjectConfigSection } from './project_config_section'\r\nimport { ReactConfigSection } from './react_config_section'\r\nimport { useAppTheme } from '../../theme/use_app_theme'\r\nimport {\r\n    cloneMarkdownStyleConfig,\r\n    isMarkdownStyleConfig,\r\n    isMarkdownStylePresetName,\r\n    type MarkdownStyleConfig,\r\n    type MarkdownStyleName,\r\n} from '../../theme/theme_config'\r\nimport { MarkdownConfigSection } from './markdown_config_section'\r\n\r\nconst CONFIG_PAGE_PADDING = 3\r\nconst CONFIG_FORM_MAX_WIDTH = 720\r\nconst CONFIG_SIDEBAR_WIDTH = 220\r\nconst DRAFT_DISCARD_DELAY_MS = 0\r\nconst MARKDOWN_CONFIG_SECTION = { id: 'markdown', label: 'Markdown' }\r\n\r\ninterface MarkdownStyleDraft {\r\n    config: MarkdownStyleConfig\r\n    name: MarkdownStyleName\r\n}\r\n\r\ninterface ConfigPageProps {\r\n    hash: string\r\n}\r\n\r\nfunction getActiveSection(hash: string, sections: typeof CONFIG_SECTIONS) {\r\n    if (sections.length === 0) throw new Error('Config page requires at least one visible section')\r\n\r\n    const section = hash.replace('#', '')\r\n    if (sections.some((item) => item.id === section)) return section\r\n\r\n    return sections[0].id\r\n}\r\n\r\nfunction getVisibleSections(entries: ConfigEntry[]) {\r\n    return CONFIG_SECTIONS.flatMap((section) => {\r\n        const visibleSection = entries.some((entry) => entry.section === section.id) ? [section] : []\r\n        return section.id === 'react' ? [...visibleSection, MARKDOWN_CONFIG_SECTION] : visibleSection\r\n    })\r\n}\r\n\r\nfunction getConfigDraftSnapshot() {\r\n    return configService.getDraft()\r\n}\r\n\r\nfunction subscribeToConfigChanges(onStoreChange: () => void) {\r\n    configService.addEventListener('changed', onStoreChange)\r\n\r\n    return () => configService.removeEventListener('changed', onStoreChange)\r\n}\r\n\r\nexport function ConfigPage(props: ConfigPageProps) {\r\n    const { hash } = props\r\n    const theme = useTheme()\r\n    const isMobile = useMediaQuery(theme.breakpoints.down('md'))\r\n    const {\r\n        markdownStyle,\r\n        markdownStyleConfig,\r\n        setCustomMarkdownStyle,\r\n        setMarkdownStyle,\r\n    } = useAppTheme()\r\n    const draft = useSyncExternalStore(subscribeToConfigChanges, getConfigDraftSnapshot)\r\n    const [invalidConfigKeys, setInvalidConfigKeys] = useState<Set<ConfigKey>>(() => new Set())\r\n    const [markdownStyleDraft, setMarkdownStyleDraft] = useState<MarkdownStyleDraft>(() => ({\r\n        config: cloneMarkdownStyleConfig(markdownStyleConfig),\r\n        name: markdownStyle,\r\n    }))\r\n    const draftDiscardTimeoutRef = useRef<number | null>(null)\r\n    const entries = configService.getEntries()\r\n    const visibleSections = useMemo(() => getVisibleSections(entries), [entries])\r\n    const activeSection = getActiveSection(hash, visibleSections)\r\n    const markdownStyleChanged = markdownStyleDraft.name !== markdownStyle\r\n        || JSON.stringify(markdownStyleDraft.config) !== JSON.stringify(markdownStyleConfig)\r\n    const markdownStyleValid = isMarkdownStyleConfig(markdownStyleDraft.config)\r\n\r\n    useEffect(() => {\r\n        if (draftDiscardTimeoutRef.current !== null) {\r\n            window.clearTimeout(draftDiscardTimeoutRef.current)\r\n            draftDiscardTimeoutRef.current = null\r\n        }\r\n\r\n        const currentDraft = configService.getDraft()\r\n        if (!currentDraft) configService.loadDraft()\r\n        return () => {\r\n            // React StrictMode mounts, unmounts, and remounts effects; delay discard so the remount can cancel it.\r\n            draftDiscardTimeoutRef.current = window.setTimeout(() => {\r\n                configService.discardDraft()\r\n                draftDiscardTimeoutRef.current = null\r\n            }, DRAFT_DISCARD_DELAY_MS)\r\n        }\r\n    }, [])\r\n\r\n    if (!draft) return null\r\n\r\n    const handleValueChange = (key: ConfigKey, value: unknown) => {\r\n        try {\r\n            if (\r\n                key === 'project.cardSeparator'\r\n                && value !== draft[key]\r\n                && value !== configService.get('project.cardSeparator')\r\n            ) {\r\n                dialogService.warning(\r\n                    'Saving this change will rename existing card files and update their IDs.',\r\n                    { critical: true, title: 'Card files will be renamed' },\r\n                )\r\n            }\r\n            configService.setDraftValue(key, value)\r\n        } catch (error) {\r\n            dialogService.error(error, { fallbackMessage: 'Invalid config value' })\r\n        }\r\n    }\r\n\r\n    const handleValidityChange = (key: ConfigKey, valid: boolean) => {\r\n        setInvalidConfigKeys((currentKeys) => {\r\n            if (valid && !currentKeys.has(key)) return currentKeys\r\n            if (!valid && currentKeys.has(key)) return currentKeys\r\n\r\n            const nextKeys = new Set(currentKeys)\r\n            if (valid) nextKeys.delete(key)\r\n            else nextKeys.add(key)\r\n\r\n            return nextKeys\r\n        })\r\n    }\r\n\r\n    const handleMarkdownStyleChange = (name: MarkdownStyleName, config: MarkdownStyleConfig) => {\r\n        setMarkdownStyleDraft({ config, name })\r\n    }\r\n\r\n    const handleSaveClick = async () => {\r\n        try {\r\n            const shouldSaveProjectConfig = configService.hasDraftChangesForSource('project')\r\n            const shouldSaveDesktopConfig = configService.hasDraftChangesForSource('desktop')\r\n            const previousCardSeparator = configService.get('project.cardSeparator')\r\n            const nextCardSeparator = draft['project.cardSeparator']\r\n            const shouldUpdateCardSeparator = configService.hasProjectConfig()\r\n                && previousCardSeparator !== nextCardSeparator\r\n            if (shouldUpdateCardSeparator) {\r\n                await dataService.projectLoading.updateCardSeparator(previousCardSeparator, nextCardSeparator)\r\n            }\r\n            configService.saveDraft()\r\n            configService.loadDraft()\r\n            if (markdownStyleChanged && markdownStyleDraft.name === 'custom') setCustomMarkdownStyle(markdownStyleDraft.config)\r\n            else if (markdownStyleChanged && isMarkdownStylePresetName(markdownStyleDraft.name)) {\r\n                setMarkdownStyle(markdownStyleDraft.name)\r\n            }\r\n            if (shouldSaveProjectConfig && configService.hasProjectConfig()) await dataService.projectLoading.saveProjectConfig()\r\n            if (shouldSaveDesktopConfig && configService.hasDesktopConfig()) writeDesktopConfigToBridge(configService.getDesktopValues())\r\n            dialogService.success('Config saved')\r\n            navigateTo('/')\r\n        } catch (error) {\r\n            dialogService.error(error, { fallbackMessage: 'Config save failed' })\r\n        }\r\n    }\r\n\r\n    const handleCancelClick = () => {\r\n        configService.discardDraft()\r\n        navigateTo('/')\r\n    }\r\n\r\n    const sectionProps = {\r\n        draft,\r\n        entries,\r\n        onChange: handleValueChange,\r\n        onValidityChange: handleValidityChange,\r\n    }\r\n\r\n    const sectionTabs = (\r\n        <Tabs\r\n            aria-label=\"Config sections\"\r\n            orientation={isMobile ? 'horizontal' : 'vertical'}\r\n            scrollButtons=\"auto\"\r\n            value={activeSection}\r\n            variant=\"scrollable\"\r\n        >\r\n            {visibleSections.map((section) => (\r\n                <Tab component=\"a\" href={`#/config/${section.id}`} key={section.id} label={section.label} value={section.id} />\r\n            ))}\r\n        </Tabs>\r\n    )\r\n\r\n    return (\r\n        <Box\r\n            aria-label=\"Config page\"\r\n            component=\"section\"\r\n            sx={{ display: 'flex', flex: 1, minHeight: 0, overflow: 'hidden' }}\r\n        >\r\n            {!isMobile ? (\r\n                <Box\r\n                    aria-label=\"Config section navigation\"\r\n                    component=\"nav\"\r\n                    sx={{ borderRight: 1, borderColor: 'divider', flexShrink: 0, minHeight: 0, overflow: 'auto', width: CONFIG_SIDEBAR_WIDTH }}\r\n                    tabIndex={0}\r\n                >\r\n                    {sectionTabs}\r\n                </Box>\r\n            ) : null}\r\n            <Box\r\n                aria-label=\"Config section content\"\r\n                role=\"region\"\r\n                sx={{ flex: 1, minHeight: 0, minWidth: 0, overflow: 'auto', p: CONFIG_PAGE_PADDING }}\r\n                tabIndex={0}\r\n            >\r\n                <Stack spacing={3} sx={{ maxWidth: CONFIG_FORM_MAX_WIDTH }}>\r\n                    <Stack direction={{ xs: 'column', sm: 'row' }} spacing={2} sx={{ alignItems: { sm: 'center' } }}>\r\n                        <Typography component=\"h2\" sx={{ flexGrow: 1 }} variant=\"h5\">\r\n                            Config\r\n                        </Typography>\r\n                        <Button onClick={handleCancelClick} variant=\"outlined\">\r\n                            Cancel\r\n                        </Button>\r\n                        <Button disabled={invalidConfigKeys.size > 0 || !markdownStyleValid} onClick={handleSaveClick} variant=\"contained\">\r\n                            Save\r\n                        </Button>\r\n                    </Stack>\r\n\r\n                    {isMobile ? sectionTabs : null}\r\n\r\n                    {activeSection === 'react' ? <ReactConfigSection {...sectionProps} /> : null}\r\n                    {activeSection === 'markdown' ? (\r\n                        <MarkdownConfigSection\r\n                            config={markdownStyleDraft.config}\r\n                            name={markdownStyleDraft.name}\r\n                            onChange={handleMarkdownStyleChange}\r\n                        />\r\n                    ) : null}\r\n                    {activeSection === 'project' ? <ProjectConfigSection {...sectionProps} /> : null}\r\n                    {activeSection === 'desktop' ? <DesktopConfigSection {...sectionProps} disabled={!configService.hasDesktopConfig()} /> : null}\r\n                </Stack>\r\n            </Box>\r\n        </Box>\r\n    )\r\n}\r\n",

Keep ability to navigate with url when in browser\r\n\r\n## Current state\r\n\r\n- The toolbar `Config` button calls `navigateTo('/config')`, which sets `window.location.hash` to `#/config`.\r\n- `MainWindow` treats `/config` as a full-page route and replaces `ProjectWorkspace` with `ConfigPage`. The status bar is hidden while config is open.\r\n- `ConfigPage` owns the config draft lifecycle: it loads a draft on mount, discards it on unmount/cancel, saves React/project/desktop/Markdown changes, reports through `dialogService`, and navigates back to `/` after save or cancel.\r\n- Config sections are selected through hash routes like `#/config/project` and `#/config/desktop`; `app_navigation.ts` maps those hashes to `{ pathname: '/config', hash: '#project' }`.\r\n- Existing tests cover toolbar navigation, direct URL entry to `#/config/desktop`, draft behavior, save/cancel, project-config persistence, desktop bridge persistence, and responsive section tabs.\r\n\r\n## implementation details\r\n\r\n- Keep `ConfigPage` as the owner of config editing, draft state, validation, save/cancel behavior, and section rendering. Extract only if the dialog shell needs a distinct wrapper; do not duplicate config form logic.\r\n- Change the toolbar entry point so it opens config as a dialog over the current workspace instead of replacing the workspace route.\r\n- Preserve direct browser navigation: loading or navigating to `#/config` or `#/config/<section>` must still show the same config UI and select the requested section.\r\n- Closing the dialog from the toolbar flow should return to the previous workspace state without resetting the open project, active view, search state, or menu state beyond closing the dialog itself.\r\n- Saving should keep the current persistence behavior: project config writes through `dataService.projectLoading.saveProjectConfig()`, desktop config writes through `writeDesktopConfigToBridge()`, Markdown style changes use the theme settings path, and errors stay reported through `dialogService`.\r\n- The dialog should follow the existing MUI dialog conventions from `design/STYLE_GUIDE.md`: title/header, scrollable body, footer actions aligned bottom-right, outlined `Cancel`, contained `Save`, and no nested card layout.\r\n- Section links must remain URL-addressable. The dialog can update `#/config/<section>` while open, but route handling must avoid losing the underlying workspace context.\r\n\r\n## acceptance criteria\r\n\r\n- Clicking toolbar `Config` opens a modal dialog over the current workspace instead of replacing `ProjectWorkspace`.\r\n- Direct navigation to `#/config`, `#/config/react`, `#/config/markdown`, `#/config/project`, or `#/config/desktop` opens config and selects the correct section.\r\n- Save and cancel close config and restore normal workspace routing; unsaved config draft changes are discarded on cancel.\r\n- Saving preserves all current side effects for React, project, desktop, and Markdown config, including project config persistence and Electron desktop bridge persistence.\r\n- The current project, active workspace view, open files, search input, and card/list state are not reset by opening or closing config.\r\n- Mobile and desktop layouts both render the config sections inside the dialog without clipped actions or inaccessible section navigation.\r\n- Tests cover toolbar dialog open/close, direct URL open, section deep links, save/cancel routing, and preservation of workspace state behind the dialog.\r\n",

Math.max(MIN_WIDTH, parsed.width) : undefined\n    if (height === undefined && width === undefined) return null\n\n    return { height, width }\n}\n\nfunction maxPopoverHeight() {\n    return Math.max(MIN_HEIGHT, window.innerHeight - POPOVER_TOP_MARGIN - POPOVER_SIDE_MARGIN)\n}\n\nfunction maxPopoverWidth() {\n    return Math.max(MIN_WIDTH, window.innerWidth - POPOVER_SIDE_MARGIN * 2)\n}\n\nfunction directionCursor(direction: ResizeDirection) {\n    if (direction === 'top' || direction === 'bottom') return 'ns-resize'\n    if (direction === 'left' || direction === 'right') return 'ew-resize'\n    if (direction === 'top-right' || direction === 'bottom-left') return 'nesw-resize'\n    return 'nwse-resize'\n}\n\nfunction directionPosition(direction: ResizeDirection) {\n    const isCorner = direction.includes('-')\n    const touchesTop = direction.startsWith('top')\n    const touchesBottom = direction.startsWith('bottom')\n    const touchesLeft = direction.endsWith('left') || direction === 'left'\n    const touchesRight = direction.endsWith('right') || direction === 'right'\n\n    return {\n        bottom: touchesBottom ? 0 : undefined,\n        cursor: directionCursor(direction),\n        height: isCorner ? HANDLE_SIZE : touchesTop || touchesBottom ? EDGE_HANDLE_SIZE : `calc(100% - ${HANDLE_SIZE * 2}px)`,\n        left: touchesLeft ? 0 : direction === 'top' || direction === 'bottom' ? HANDLE_SIZE : undefined,\n        right: touchesRight ? 0 : undefined,\n        top: touchesTop ? 0 : direction === 'left' || direction === 'right' ? HANDLE_SIZE : undefined,\n        width: isCorner ? HANDLE_SIZE : touchesLeft || touchesRight ? EDGE_HANDLE_SIZE : `calc(100% - ${HANDLE_SIZE * 2}px)`,\n    }\n}\n\n/** An anchored popover with configurable drag handles for resizing its content. */\nexport function ResizablePopover(props: ResizablePopoverProps) {\n    const {\n        anchorElement,\n        anchorOrigin = { horizontal: 'left', vertical: 'bottom' },\n        children,\n        initialSize,\n        labelId,\n        onClose,\n        open,\n        paperSx,\n        resizeCorner = 'lower-right',\n        resizeFromAllSides = false,\n        resizeLabel,\n        sizeStorageKey,\n        transformOrigin = { horizontal: 'left', vertical: 'top' },\n    } = props\n    const [size, setSize] = useState<PopoverSize>(() => readStoredSize(sizeStorageKey) ?? initialSize)\n    const paperRef = useRef<HTMLDivElement | null>(null)\n    const resizeRef = useRef<AbortController | null>(null)\n\n    useEffect(() => () => resizeRef.current?.abort(), [])\n\n    const handleClose = (_event: unknown, reason: 'backdropClick' | 'escapeKeyDown') => {\n        resizeRef.current?.abort()\n        onClose(reason)\n    }\n\n    const startResize = (event: ReactPointerEvent) => {\n        event.preventDefault()\n        resizeRef.current?.abort()\n\n        if (!paperRef.current) throw new Error('Missing resizable popover paper element')\n\n        const direction = event.currentTarget.getAttribute('data-direction') as ResizeDirection | null\n        const controller = new AbortController()\n        const bounds = paperRef.current.getBoundingClientRect()\n        const start = {\n            height: size.height ?? bounds.height,\n            width: size.width ?? bounds.width,\n            x: event.clientX,\n            y: event.clientY,\n        }\n        resizeRef.current = controller\n\n        window.addEventListener('pointermove', (move: PointerEvent) => {\n            const activeDirection = direction ?? (resizeCorner === 'lower-left' ? 'bottom-left' : 'bottom-right')\n            const horizontalDelta = move.clientX - start.x\n            const verticalDelta = move.clientY - start.y\n            const resizesLeft = activeDirection.includes('left')\n            const resizesRight = activeDirection.includes('right')\n            const resizesTop = activeDirection.includes('top')\n            const resizesBottom = activeDirection.includes('bottom')\n            const width = Math.max(MIN_WIDTH, start.width + (resizesLeft ? -horizontalDelta : resizesRight ? horizontalDelta : 0))\n            const height = Math.max(MIN_HEIGHT, start.height + (resizesTop ? -verticalDelta : resizesBottom ? verticalDelta : 0))\n\n            setSize({ height: Math.min(height, maxPopoverHeight()), width: Math.min(width, maxPopoverWidth()) })\n        }, { signal: controller.signal })\n        window.addEventListener('pointerup', () => {\n            controller.abort()\n            if (sizeStorageKey && paperRef.current) {\n                const paperBounds = paperRef.current.getBoundingClientRect()\n                window.localStorage.setItem(sizeStorageKey, JSON.stringify({ height: paperBounds.height, width: paperBounds.width }))\n            }\n        }, { signal: controller.signal })\n    }\n\n    return (\n        <Popover\n            anchorEl={anchorElement}\n            anchorOrigin={anchorOrigin}\n            marginThreshold={POPOVER_TOP_MARGIN}\n            onClose={handleClose}\n            open={open}\n            slotProps={{\n                paper: {\n                    'aria-labelledby': labelId,\n                    ref: paperRef,\n                    role: 'dialog',\n                    style: size,\n                    sx: [{\n                        display: 'flex',\n                        maxHeight: `calc(100vh - ${POPOVER_TOP_MARGIN + POPOVER_SIDE_MARGIN}px)`,\n                        maxWidth: `calc(100vw - ${POPOVER_SIDE_MARGIN * 2}px)`,\n                        overflow: 'hidden',\n                        position: 'relative',\n                    }, paperSx] as SxProps<Theme>,\n                },\n            }}\n            transformOrigin={transformOrigin}\n        >\n            {children}\n            {resizeFromAllSides ? ALL_RESIZE_DIRECTIONS.map((direction) => (\n                <Box\n                    aria-label={`${resizeLabel} from ${direction}`}\n                    data-direction={direction}\n                    key={direction}\n                    onPointerDown={startResize}\n                    role=\"separator\"\n                    sx={{ ...directionPosition(direction), position: 'absolute', touchAction: 'none' }}\n                />\n            )) : (\n                <Box\n                    aria-label={resizeLabel}\n                    data-corner={resizeCorner}\n                    onPointerDown={startResize}\n                    role=\"separator\"\n                    sx={{\n                        bottom: 0,\n                        cursor: resizeCorner === 'lower-left' ? 'nesw-resize' : 'nwse-resize',\n                        height: HANDLE_SIZE,\n                        left: resizeCorner === 'lower-left' ? 0 : undefined,\n                        position: 'absolute',\n                        right: resizeCorner === 'lower-right' ? 0 : undefined,\n                        touchAction: 'none',\n                        width: HANDLE_SIZE,\n                    }}\n                />\n            )}\n        </Popover>\n    )\n}\n\r\n",
design\activity\card__3e151ae1-ffa3-42ba-819c-a6973683af03.json:52:          "content": "---\ninternalId: f2ec9e28-8064-4707-bce9-b62f24d57524\n---\n\n# App Style Guide â€” Kanban / MDÂ² (React + MUI)\n\nHow to build **any new component** so it matches the app. This is written for **Material UI v5+** components.\n\n**The theme is the source of truth.** All color, radius, base typography, and spacing units live in the single `createTheme` (defined in `GUIDANCE.md` Â§1/Â§9). This guide does **not** define colors â€” it tells you **which theme value to use for which role**, and covers the things the theme can't encode: layout, spacing/margins, borders, elevation, and component conventions.\n\n**The one rule that matters:** never write a raw hex, px radius, or magic color into a component. Read it from the theme (`theme.palette.*`, `theme.shape`, `theme.typography`, `theme.spacing`). If a component has a hardcoded hex in its `sx`/styled, it's wrong â€” that's exactly where the look drifts and where dark mode breaks.\n\n---\n\n## 1. How to consume the theme\n\n- **Colors:** `sx={{ color: 'text.secondary', bgcolor: 'background.paper', borderColor: 'divider' }}` â€” MUI resolves dotted palette paths automatically in `sx`. In `styled`/JS use the callback form: `styled(Box)(({ theme }) => ({ color: theme.palette.text.secondary }))`.\n- **Spacing:** use the 8px unit via the spacing scale â€” `sx={{ p: 2, gap: 1, mt: 1.5 }}` (`2` = 16px, `1` = 8px). Don't write `padding: '16px'`.\n- **Radius:** `borderRadius: 1` (= `theme.shape.borderRadius` = 8) and multiples; for the fixed non-8 radii see Â§4.\n- **Typography:** prefer `Typography variant=...` and `theme.typography.*` over ad-hoc `fontSize`.\n- **Custom tokens:** roles the default MUI palette doesn't cover (column/track surfaces, the strong/hover border steps, `text-3/4`, section-header color, `primary-bg` tint, status colors) must exist in the theme under a namespace (e.g. `theme.palette.custom.*`) with light + dark values. Consume them the same way â€” `bgcolor: 'custom.column'`. **Never inline their hex.** If a needed token doesn't exist yet, add it to the theme, don't hardcode it in the component.\n\n---\n\n## 2. Role â†’ theme slot\n\nPick the slot by the element's **role**, not by how it looks in one mode:\n\n| Role | Theme slot |\n|---|---|\n| App background; tinted footer/action bars | `background.default` |\n| Column & sidebar surface | `custom.column` |\n| Segmented-control / toolbar track, hover fill | `custom.track` |\n| Card, dialog, popup, input surface | `background.paper` |\n| Hairlines, resting borders | `divider` |\n| Input borders, vertical separators | `custom.borderStrong` |\n| Border on hover | `custom.borderHover` |\n| Titles, values, headings | `text.primary` |\n| Body copy, field labels | `text.secondary` |\n| Meta, captions, resting icons | `custom.text3` |\n| Muted / placeholder / disabled | `custom.text4` |\n| Uppercase section/column headers | `custom.colHead` |\n| The one CTA, selection, focus, links, icon-hover | `primary.main` |\n| Contained-button hover | `primary.dark` |\n| Selected/tinted bg, focus ring, ID-chip bg | `custom.primaryBg` |\n| Text/icon on a primary fill | `primary.contrastText` |\n| Active / saved / online dot | `success.main` |\n| Destructive action | `error.main` |\n| Status swatch dots & ID-chip tints (decorative only) | `custom.status.*` |\n\nRules: **one** `primary` per surface (the CTA/selection accent) â€” everything else is `text-*`/`divider`. Status colors are **decoration only** (dots, chip tints), never interactive color. Dark-mode brightness/tinting is handled inside the theme's two palettes, so a correctly-sloted component needs zero per-mode code.\n\n---\n\n## 3. Layout\n\n- **Full-height app:** column flex â€” menu row / ribbon / content (`flex: 1; minHeight: 0`) / status bar. Fixed bands `flexShrink: 0`.\n- **Board:** horizontal-scroll flex row, `gap: 2` (16px), page padding `p: 2.5` (20px); columns `width: 296, flexShrink: 0`, internal column flex `gap: 1`.\n- **List view:** two-pane flex row filling the space between ribbon and status bar â€” sidebar `width: 280, flexShrink: 0`, editor pane `flex: 1, minWidth: 0` (the `minWidth: 0` is required so long content ellipsizes instead of blowing out the row).\n- **Panels (sidebar, editor card, dialogs):** column flex with stacked bands (header / [toolbar] / body / footer). The **body scrolls** (`overflow-y: auto; minHeight: 0`); header and footer are `flexShrink: 0` and never scroll away.\n- **Spacer pattern:** push trailing items with `<Box sx={{ flex: 1 }} />` rather than `margin-left: auto` sprinkled around, so rows stay predictable.\n- Use flex `gap` for spacing between siblings â€” don't hand-space with per-child margins.\n\n---\n\n## 4. Spacing, margin & size conventions\n\n- **4/8px grid, via `theme.spacing`.** page padding `2.5`; between columns `2`; inside columns / between related controls `1`; dialog body gap `2â€“2.25`; field labelâ†’control gap `~0.9` (7px).\n- **Margins:** prefer padding on containers + flex `gap` over element margins. Where a floating panel needs breathing room (e.g. editor card, toolbar inside a panel), use container padding (`p: 2 / 2.5`), not margins on the children.\n- **Fixed heights (px):** menu row 44, ribbon 52, status bar 32, section header 40, tab row 40, standard button / control 34, dense icon button 26â€“28, input 42.\n- **Fixed widths (px):** column 296, sidebar 280, search 260, standard dialog 480, wide/editor dialog 760.\n- **Radius family (px):** buttons/icon-buttons 8 (small 6â€“7), inputs 9, cards 10, columns/panels 12, dialogs/popups 14, chips/pills 99, color swatches 3. `borderRadius: 1` covers the 8 case; use explicit `'9px'` etc. for the others.\n\n---\n\n## 5. Borders & elevation\n\n- **Rest = border, not shadow.** Resting surfaces: `border: '1px solid'`, `borderColor: 'divider'`. Inputs use `custom.borderStrong`. **Shadow only when floating or lifted** (hover, drag, dialogs/popovers).\n- **Separation between bands:** a single 1px `divider` hairline. Don't stack a heavy rule *and* an outline â€” one line, let background contrast do the rest. Vertical separators inside toolbars: a 20px-tall `custom.borderStrong` rule.\n- **Elevation ladder (only where floating):** card hover `0 4px 12px rgba(16,24,40,0.12)`; dragging MUI `elevation 8` + `rotate(2deg)`; contained button `0 1px 2px rgba(16,24,40,0.15)`; dialog/popup `0 24px 60px rgba(16,24,40,0.28)`; scrim `rgba(16,24,40,0.45)` + `backdropFilter: blur(2px)`.\n- Set `MuiPaper.elevation: 0` and `MuiButton.disableElevation` globally in the theme; add the shadows above explicitly where the ladder calls for it.\n- **On dark backgrounds shadows read as nothing** â€” the theme already handles this by making hover raise `borderColor` (`custom.borderHover`) instead of relying on shadow.\n\n---\n\n## 6. Typography usage\n\nDrive everything from theme variants / `theme.typography`; avoid ad-hoc `fontSize`.\n\n- Titles/values/headings â†’ `text.primary`; body & labels â†’ `text.secondary`; meta â†’ `custom.text3`.\n- **Field labels:** a plain `Typography` (12px/600, `text.secondary`) placed **above** the control â€” **never** MUI floating/outlined `TextField` labels (they clash with the app's flat-label style).\n- **Section/column headers:** `Typography variant=\"overline\"` (uppercase, `letterSpacing ~0.7px`, `fontWeight 700`, `custom.colHead`).\n- **ID chips only** use monospace; everything else is the theme's default family.\n- `button.textTransform: 'none'` and `button.fontWeight: 600` are set in the theme â€” don't re-uppercase buttons.\n\n---\n\n## 7. Interaction states\n\nConsistent across all components; all colors from the theme:\n\n- **Ghost icon button** (`IconButton`): transparent â†’ hover `bgcolor: track` (or `background.paper` on a colored panel) + `color: primary.main`. Override MUI's default circular hover tint via `sx`.\n- **Outlined button:** `divider` border, `text.secondary` â†’ hover `borderColor/color: primary.main`. Destructive: hover `borderColor: error.main` + `bgcolor: custom.dangerBg`.\n- **Contained (primary) CTA:** `primary.main` + small shadow â†’ hover `primary.dark`.\n- **Input/field focus:** `borderColor: primary.main` + `boxShadow: 0 0 0 3px` in `custom.primaryBg` (the soft halo). Unfocused hover: `borderColor: custom.borderHover`.\n- **List/tree row:** hover `bgcolor: track`; selected `bgcolor: custom.primaryBg` + title `text.primary`.\n- **Row-level actions** (delete, â‹®): hidden at rest, shown on `:hover`/`:focus-within` via **opacity** (keep in DOM so width doesn't jump).\n- **Active tab/menu item:** 2px `primary.main` bottom border + `primary.main` text.\n- Every icon-only control gets a `Tooltip` (theme sets `arrow: true`) **and** an `aria-label`.\n\n---\n\n## 8. Component conventions (MUI primitives)\n\n- **Buttons:** `Button variant=\"contained\"` = the single CTA per surface; `variant=\"outlined\"` = secondary; `variant=\"text\"` = tertiary. Icon-only â†’ `IconButton` in a `Tooltip`. Don't use `Link` or text `Button` where an action button belongs (that reproduces the old text-link look).\n- **Icons:** `@mui/icons-material` **Outlined** variants; `fontSize: 18` in 34px buttons, `16` in dense, `13â€“15` inline. Don't hand-draw SVG.\n- **ID chip:** monospace, accent text on `custom.primaryBg`/status tint, `radius 5, flexShrink: 0`.\n- **Count chip:** `background.paper` bg, 1px `divider`, radius 9â€“10, `custom.text3`.\n- **State dot:** 7â€“8px circle + `text-3` label; green (`success.main`) = active/saved/online.\n- **Search:** pill `TextField` (`borderRadius: 99`, `bgcolor: background.default`), search start-adornment, `âŒ˜K` keycap end-adornment.\n- **Select:** `size=\"small\"`, optional dot+name via `renderValue`; 42px / radius-9 frame. When a select has a tooltip, keep the tooltip available while the select is closed and explicitly hide it for the entire time the select menu is open so it cannot cover the first option.\n- **Segmented control** (view switch, formatting toolbar): `ToggleButtonGroup` on a `custom.track` background; selected segment `background.paper` + `0 1px 2px` shadow + `primary` text.\n- **Dialog / popup:** `Dialog`/`Popover` with `PaperProps` â†’ `background.paper`, 1px `divider`, radius 14, big shadow; scrim via `slotProps.backdrop` (blur + tint). Bands separated by hairlines; footer on a `background.default` bar with top hairline; actions right-aligned (outlined Cancel + contained CTA). `autoFocus` first field; submit on `Enter` (`âŒ˜/Ctrl+Enter` in a textarea); close on `Esc`/backdrop.\n- **Empty state:** dashed target â€” `1.5px dashed custom.borderStrong`, radius 10, centered icon + `custom.text4` label. No \"click to add\" placeholder blocks.\n\n---\n\n## 9. Definition of done for a new component\n\n1. Zero hardcoded hex / raw px colors â€” every value comes from `theme.palette` / `theme.shape` / `theme.spacing` / `theme.typography`.\n2. Correct roleâ†’slot mapping (Â§2); at most one `primary` CTA on the surface.\n3. Borders at rest, shadow only when floating (Â§5); bands split by a single hairline.\n4. Hover **and** focus states on every interactive element (Â§7); icon buttons have tooltip + `aria-label`.\n5. Body scrolls, header/footer pinned; `minWidth: 0` on flex children that hold long text.\n6. Toggle to dark mode and confirm nothing breaks â€” if it does, you hardcoded a color somewhere (Â§1).\n\nComponent-specific detail lives in `GUIDANCE.md` (theme definition + board/list/dialog), `CARD_POPUP_GUIDE.md`, `RUN_DIALOG_GUIDE.md`, and `SIDEBAR_ACTIONS_GUIDE.md`.\n\r\n---\ninternalId: 583d9c88-b71c-4560-92ad-3e23d33bf1d0\n---\n\n# Architectural decisions\n\nProject-wide decisions for MDÂ². The app is a Vite React web app in `app/`; `desktop/` is a separate Electron host that can load the website and expose local capabilities through preload bridges.\n\n## File naming\n\n| Decision | Rule | Rationale |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| Code files use lowercase snake_case names. | All code files in `app/src/` and `desktop/` use lowercase words separated by underscores, for example `github_auth_service.ts`, `project_workspace.tsx`, and `local_git_service.js`. Test files keep the same base name with `.test` before the extension, for example `github_auth_service.test.ts`. Exported symbols keep normal TypeScript/JavaScript casing such as `GithubAuthService`, `ProjectWorkspace`, and `useGithubAuth`. | A single file naming convention avoids mixed PascalCase, camelCase, and hyphenated filenames, and keeps imports predictable across Windows and case-sensitive environments. |\n\n## Services and state\n\n| Decision | Rule | Rationale |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| Global singleton services own domain state and logic. | Each domain is a class in `src/services/**`, instantiated once at module level and exported, for example `export const indexesService = new IndexesService()`. React components do not own domain state. | Keeps business logic out of components, testable without a DOM, and shared across windows/views without Redux, Zustand, or Context stores. |\n| Service location follows usage scope. | If a service is specific to one UI element and used only there, place it beside that component. Generic or shared services, such as logging, database access, config, storage, or cross-screen domain logic, belong in `src/services/`. | Keeps component-owned behavior local while preserving `src/services/` for reusable application services. |\n| Consumers use direct imports or the service injector. | Direct import when no import cycle exists; use `src/services/service_injector.js` when a cycle would occur. Every global singleton service registers itself in its constructor with `inj.register('myService', this)`. | The service graph is dense; the injector is a bare global registry that defers resolution to call time. |\n| Services have a two-phase lifecycle. | Constructors only register and set unloaded state such as `null`. Config-dependent or service-dependent work runs in `init()`, `start()`, app bootstrap (`App.jsx`), or a `loaded` lifecycle event. `configService.config` is private; callers use `get`, `set`, and `clear`. | Module evaluation order is not guaranteed, so `configService` is not usable at import time. Reading config in a constructor is a bug. |\n\n\n## Events and React integration\n\n| Decision | Rule | Rationale |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| Services notify observers through their own `EventTarget`. | Services expose an `EventTarget` and dispatch named `CustomEvent` domain events such as `activeIndex`, `added`, `deleted`, or `changedBox`. Observers subscribe with `addEventListener` and unsubscribe with `removeEventListener` on the owning service. | Decouples producers from consumers without depending on Node `EventEmitter`, which is not available in the browser-first React app. |\n| Custom hooks bridge service events to functional components. | Hooks in `src/components/hooks/`, such as `useActiveIndex` and `useProjectConfig`, seed `useState` from a service property, subscribe in `useEffect`, unsubscribe in cleanup, and return the value. Prefer hook + service over prop chains. | Components stay declarative and avoid direct event plumbing. |\n| Components subscribe at the smallest rendering boundary. | Root and layout components compose UI regions and pass structural inputs. Components that render changing application data subscribe through hooks themselves. Do not hoist changing data into ancestors only to pass it downward. | Limits rerenders to affected UI, protects transient state such as open popups, and avoids broad prop chains. |\n| Components use the app theme service path. | `App` owns theme mode through `useThemeMode()`, builds the MUI theme with `createAppTheme(mode)`, and provides it through `ThemeProvider`. Components read theme values with MUI APIs such as `useTheme`, `useMediaQuery`, and `sx`; only controls that change the palette mode receive `mode` and `onToggleTheme`. | Theme state, persistence, and palette construction stay centralized while components remain presentation-focused. |\n\r\n---\r\nid: F-061\r\ntitle: Select workTree from action popup\r\nstatus: ready\r\nowner: JB\r\naffects:\r\npolicy:\r\n  checkLinting: true\r\n  requireTests: true\r\ninternalId: 3f683f00-ed34-40a8-afeb-9932e62b4b34\r\n---\r\n\r\n## Goal\nUser can select the active worktree from the action popup. When the action popup is associated to a card, it reflects the worktree of that card (and also updates it). When the action popup is for the project agent, then the user can select the worktree on which to run the agent project wide.\n\n## Current state\n\n- The popup header contains the action selector, expand, and close controls in one row; it has no worktree control.\n- Card worktree assignments are stored in frontmatter and included in card action contexts. The project-agent context has no worktree assignment.\n- Electron uses a card's valid assignment only when an action has `needsWorkTree`. It rejects project contexts for such actions; actions without `needsWorkTree` run in the primary worktree.\n\n## implementation details\n\n- Add an accessible worktree icon/menu at the upper left, on the same row as the right-aligned expand and close buttons. Move the action selector to a second row.\n- List only valid linked worktrees reported by Git, plus an unassigned option. Keep invalid card assignments visible with their existing error.\n- In card context, initialize from the card assignment and persist changes through `updateCardWorktree`; keep the previous selection if saving fails.\n- Disable linked worktrees reserved by another active card. Background cards do not reserve worktrees.\n- Before persisting a card assignment, Electron creates a title-slug branch in the selected clean worktree from the opened project branch. Existing branches and dirty worktrees fail without changing the assignment.\n- In project context, keep the assignment in renderer service state for the current opened-project session only. Reset it when the project closes or changes; do not write it to project files, config, or schedules.\n- Project context can select any valid linked worktree, including one reserved by an active card, and does not prepare a branch.\n- Use the effective assignment for action filtering, prompt preparation, and execution. Electron resolves it only when `needsWorkTree` is true, accepting card or project context; missing, invalid, or unavailable assignments fail before process start. Actions without `needsWorkTree` still run in the primary worktree.\n- Disable assignment changes while an action is running. # Architectural decisions

Project-wide decisions for MDÂ². The app is a Vite React web app in `app/`; `desktop/` is a separate Electron host that can load the website and expose local capabilities through preload bridges.

## File naming

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Code files use lowercase snake_case names. | All code files in `app/src/` and `desktop/` use lowercase words separated by underscores, for example `github_auth_service.ts`, `project_workspace.tsx`, and `local_git_service.js`. Test files keep the same base name with `.test` before the extension, for example `github_auth_service.test.ts`. Exported symbols keep normal TypeScript/JavaScript casing such as `GithubAuthService`, `ProjectWorkspace`, and `useGithubAuth`. | A single file naming convention avoids mixed PascalCase, camelCase, and hyphenated filenames, and keeps imports predictable across Windows and case-sensitive environments. |

## Services and state

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Global singleton services own domain state and logic. | Each domain is a class in `src/services/**`, instantiated once at module level and exported, for example `export const indexesService = new IndexesService()`. React components do not own domain state. | Keeps business logic out of components, testable without a DOM, and shared across windows/views without Redux, Zustand, or Context stores. |
| Service location follows usage scope. | If a service is specific to one UI element and used only there, place it beside that component. Generic or shared services, such as logging, database access, config, storage, or cross-screen domain logic, belong in `src/services/`. | Keeps component-owned behavior local while preserving `src/services/` for reusable application services. |
| Consumers use direct imports or the service injector. | Direct import when no import cycle exists; use `src/services/service_injector.js` when a cycle would occur. Every global singleton service registers itself in its constructor with `inj.register('myService', this)`. | The service graph is dense; the injector is a bare global registry that defers resolution to call time. |
| Services have a two-phase lifecycle. | Constructors only register and set unloaded state such as `null`. Config-dependent or service-dependent work runs in `init()`, `start()`, app bootstrap (`App.jsx`), or a `loaded` lifecycle event. `configService.config` is private; callers use `get`, `set`, and `clear`. | Module evaluation order is not guaranteed, so `configService` is not usable at import time. Reading config in a constructor is a bug. |


## Events and React integration

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Services notify observers through their own `EventTarget`. | Services expose an `EventTarget` and dispatch named `CustomEvent` domain events such as `activeIndex`, `added`, `deleted`, or `changedBox`. # Architectural decisions

Project-wide decisions for MDÂ². The app is a Vite React web app in `app/`; `desktop/` is a separate Electron host that can load the website and expose local capabilities through preload bridges.

## File naming

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Code files use lowercase snake_case names. | All code files in `app/src/` and `desktop/` use lowercase words separated by underscores, for example `github_auth_service.ts`, `project_workspace.tsx`, and `local_git_service.js`. Test files keep the same base name with `.test` before the extension, for example `github_auth_service.test.ts`. Exported symbols keep normal TypeScript/JavaScript casing such as `GithubAuthService`, `ProjectWorkspace`, and `useGithubAuth`. | A single file naming convention avoids mixed PascalCase, camelCase, and hyphenated filenames, and keeps imports predictable across Windows and case-sensitive environments. |

## Services and state

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Global singleton services own domain state and logic. | Each domain is a class in `src/services/**`, instantiated once at module level and exported, for example `export const indexesService = new IndexesService()`. React components do not own domain state. | Keeps business logic out of components, testable without a DOM, and shared across windows/views without Redux, Zustand, or Context stores. |
| Service location follows usage scope. | If a service is specific to one UI element and used only there, place it beside that component. Generic or shared services, such as logging, database access, config, storage, or cross-screen domain logic, belong in `src/services/`. | Keeps component-owned behavior local while preserving `src/services/` for reusable application services. |
| Consumers use direct imports or the service injector. | Direct import when no import cycle exists; use `src/services/service_injector.js` when a cycle would occur. Every global singleton service registers itself in its constructor with `inj.register('myService', this)`. | The service graph is dense; the injector is a bare global registry that defers resolution to call time. |
| Services have a two-phase lifecycle. | Constructors only register and set unloaded state such as `null`. Config-dependent or service-dependent work runs in `init()`, `start()`, app bootstrap (`App.jsx`), or a `loaded` lifecycle event. `configService.config` is private; callers use `get`, `set`, and `clear`. | Module evaluation order is not guaranteed, so `configService` is not usable at import time. Reading config in a constructor is a bug. |

| --- | --- | --- |
